sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-GFP pull-down from HEK293 lysate co-transfected with FLAG-FLRT2, Myc-Lphn3, and HA-Unc5D-mVenus demonstrated that full-length Unc5D pulls down both Lphn3 and FLRT2, confirming cell-surface expression and participation in a ternary complex (L3). L2 additionally reports surface detection via the HA tag.
sites.rationale: FLRT2 is a type-I single-pass transmembrane protein with signal peptide residues 1–35; the mature extracellular domain begins at residue 36. The only extracellular terminus is the N-terminus, so an N-terminal tag must be placed after residue 35 (insert_after_residue=35, residue_before=A, residue_after=C). Python verification confirms seq[34]='A' and seq[35]='C'. L3 demonstrates the FLAG-tagged construct is functional at the cell surface (ternary complex pull-down); L2 independently corroborates the same N-terminal position with an HA tag. The tag site is 506 residues from the TM boundary, posing no steric conflict. FLAG-FLRT2 full-length construct expressed in HEK293 cells (L3); HA-tagged full-length FLRT2 transmembrane construct with tag placed after the vector secretion signal sequence (L2). Both constructs are membrane-anchored and place the tag at the extracellular N-terminus after signal-peptide cleavage. No specific residue number is stated in either paper; position is derived from the single extracellular terminus (mature N-terminus at residue 36, after SP cleavage at residue 35).

sources.claim: To verify that full-length cell surface Lphn3, FLRT2 and Unc5D form a ternary complex, we performed an anti-GFP pull-down from lysate of cells transfected with a full-length HA-Unc5D mono-Venus (mV) fusion protein, Myc-Lphn3 and FLAG-FLRT2, showing that full-length Unc5D can pull down both Lphn3 and FLRT2 ( Fig. 2f ).

literature_notes: L1 (mVenus C-terminal fusion, residues 35–660) places the fluorescent tag after residue 660, which falls in the intracellular domain (563–660); it is recorded in other_positions. L2 and L3 both pin the same N-terminal junction (after SP cleavage at residue 35); since they converge on one junction rather than two distinct ones, a single site is reported, grounded in L3 (stronger functional evidence) with L2 noted in the rationale. No internal extracellular loop insertions are supported by any ledger line.

literature_other_positions.note: Full-length FLRT2 (residues 35–660) was fused to mVenus and a polyhistidine tag at the C-terminus; residue 660 lies within the intracellular domain (563–660), making this an intracellular tag, not a surface tag.
